I farm only 10.1 mu, and our house has just two people, with some going out to work, so I cannot spread myself too thin. I still keep most of the land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the steady way here. Even if one season is not so good, the other can still bring grain and money. I leave a smaller piece for cotton because I have grown it many years and know how to manage it, but cotton takes more watching and more picking, so I do not put too much land into it. I do not like making big changes at my age. I mostly do what worked on my own fields before, and I watch costs carefully because fertilizer, water, and hired hands all need cash.

For wheat, I will sow in early October after I clear the land, using the common seed I can buy nearby, not the expensive kind. I will put a fair base fertilizer before sowing, then add one more round in spring if the wheat looks weak or yellow. Wheat cannot be short of water, so I will irrigate about three times if rain is normal. After wheat harvest in June, I will plant maize right away on the same 6.5 mu. The gap is very short, so I will not do heavy tillage, just quick field cleaning and sowing. For maize I still use hybrid seed because the stand is better. I feed it once at planting and once when it grows fast. Cotton is on the other 3.6 mu. I keep cotton because I know the field and the work, but I will not spend too much on it this year. I will use moderate fertilizer, one or two irrigations depending on rain, and spray only when I really see insects or weeds. That way I keep some cash in hand and do not overreach.
